claims.claim: There is an explicit packing of 518 A10 rectangles in one A1 rectangle.
claims.evidence: The three coordinate families contain respectively 2·32=64, 14, and 20·22=440 rectangles, totaling 518. Their dimensions are respectively 37×26, 37×26, and 26×37. They occupy [0,74]×[0,832], [74,592]×[0,26], and [74,594]×[26,840], all contained in [0,594]×[0,841]; the three regions have disjoint interiors, and each family is a regular nonoverlapping grid. The exact checker generated every rectangle and independently checked dimensions, containment, uniqueness, and every occupied unit cell. It found 498316=518·37·26 occupied cells, no multiply occupied cell, and 1238 uncovered container cells.
claims.search_method: Generated all 518 rectangles from the formulas and exhaustively marked their unit cells using Python arbitrary-precision integer coordinates and a byte occupancy map.

claims.claim: No packing can contain 519 A10 rectangles; a ten-residue periodic marker certificate gives the upper bound 518.
claims.evidence: The reduction from real to integer coordinates is valid. For any real packing, fix vertical coordinates and orientations. The feasible horizontal-coordinate set is nonempty, closed, and bounded, so the sum of horizontal coordinates has a minimizer. At that minimizer, any rectangle with x>0 must touch on its left a rectangle whose vertical interior overlaps it; otherwise finite positive clearance permits a left shift. A blocker chain strictly decreases x, must terminate at x=0, and expresses every x as a sum of widths 26 and 37, hence as an integer. Freezing these x-coordinates and repeating the compact-minimization argument vertically makes every y integral while preserving feasibility. For integer placements, the checker verified that each of the 37 cyclic intervals of length 26 contains 7 or 8 residues from each coordinate projection of P. It also exhaustively checked all 455328 placements of size 37×26 and all 458045 placements of size 26×37; every placement contains 7 or 8 markers. Direct grid counting and independent residue-multiplicity counting both give 3632 container markers. Interior-disjoint integer rectangles cover disjoint unit cells, so 519 rectangles would require at least 519·7=3633 distinct markers, which is impossible. Thus every packing has at most floor(3632/7)=518 rectangles.
claims.witness: P={(3,3),(7,25),(10,14),(14,7),(18,29),(22,11),(25,33),(29,22),(33,36),(36,18)} modulo 37. The container has exactly 3632 markers, while 519 rectangles would require 3633.
claims.search_method: Proved the real-to-integer compacting lemma from scratch; enumerated all 37 cyclic starts for both residue projections; constructed the complete marker grid; counted markers both directly and by residue multiplicities; and used exact-integer prefix sums to inspect every integer placement in both orientations.

target_evidence: The exact target asks whether the maximum for literal ISO A10 rectangles in an ISO A1 rectangle is 258 or 259. The supplied dimensions are A10=26×37 and A1=594×841. The verified placement and upper-bound certificate establish the stronger exact result OPT(594,841,37,26)=518, so the target's 258-or-259 dichotomy is false rather than merely undecided. This directly resolves the entire literal target at exact strength and supplies both requested certificate types. The draft's claimed_resolution of FULL is therefore ACCURATE.
